title: The per-service database login name for rwb-document is not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 4 and slide 8 (one login and connection pool per service); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-02
description: The architecture fixes one database login per service in the ACE PostgreSQL server, but no source document names the rwb-document login, its grants or its connection pool size. The app story can build against the rwb-document login as a placeholder and the DB story creates it, but the name and the grants are missing.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 4 (every service has schema rwb_<name> + DB login) and slide 8 notes (19 Recovery schemas, one login and connection pool each); no login name given in the TSD P5, the FSD P5, the legacy story RWB-E1-024 or the Ownership Map
proposed: Name the rwb-document login and its grants in the rwb_document DB story, following DP-02; until then the app story refers to the rwb-document login (DP-02)

title: The storage account, the container names and the WORM policy of the platform storage product are not fixed in the sources
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 (rwb-document FILE Azure Blob WORM) and slide 8 (documents in Blob with WORM); legacy story RWB-E1-024 sections 3 and 13 (containers rwb-docs, rwb-docs-legal, rwb-quarantine); RWB-PLT-TE012-APP
description: The architecture puts the files in Azure Blob with WORM through rwb-document and the legacy story names three containers, but no source fixes the storage account, the per-environment container naming, the immutability policy period or the managed identity assignment. The app story carries the legacy container names and the path {container}/{caseId}/{documentId}/v1 and calls the storage product; the account and the policy remain with the platform storage story.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 (FILE Azure Blob (WORM): files, 2.8 TB by 2031) and slide 8 notes (documents in Blob with WORM); legacy story RWB-E1-024 precondition RWB-TE-012, flow step 7 and solution plan; no storage account or policy document in the sources read
proposed: RWB-PLT-TE012-APP states the storage account, the three container names per environment, the immutability policy period per retention class and the managed identity; this story keeps the names as properties

title: The request and response field names of the store operations and the not-found message are not specified
source: TSD P5 Document hub v2 appendix T-A.2 (API-P5-001, -003, -004, -005 name the operations but not every field); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 (REST POST /documents returns the upload link); Template and Rules v1 R9
description: The TSD fixes operation paths, authorization and error codes, and names the Document response shape, but the request field names of the upload create and of the store command, the upload-link object and the message ID for a document that does not exist are not given in any source read. The story fixes the paths and the operation list and leaves the field names and the 404 message to the contract story.
evidence: TSD P5 Document hub v2 appendix T-A.2 rows API-P5-001 to API-P5-005; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 rwb-document IN line; legacy story RWB-E1-024 section 12 names the Published interface methods but not the REST request bodies; no message ID for 404 in section 14 of the legacy story
proposed: The rwb-document contract stories publish the OpenAPI for the five operations with the request and response field names and a not-found message ID; until then the story uses the TSD Document shape and an unnamed 404 problem response

title: Request and response field names of the three SCR-30 operations, the per-service login name and the text of MSG-GEN-006 are not fixed in the sources
source: Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7, RWB E1 026 Attach and search screen v1; TSD P5 Document hub v2 appendix T-A; FSD P5 Document hub v3 A2.4
description: Legacy RWB-E1-026 names the three operations and their query parameters but not the JSON field-by-field shape of Document, DocumentPage and DocumentChecklist. The plan has no P5 CON story for this legacy key, so no published contract fixes the names; the P5 store is RWB-P5-E1024-APP, an APP story whose own shapes are also unpublished. The same gap covers the name of the per-service database login (DP-02) and the wording of MSG-GEN-006 for this capability.
evidence: TSD P5 v2 T-A.2 API-P5-001/002/008 give request classes by name only (Document, DocumentPage, DocumentChecklist); the API Specification v4 has no P5 contract story in the split plan; the FSD gives MSG-GEN-006 at AC-EXC-P5-001-03 without a text for the virus-scan case.
owner_role: Solution architect, with the P5 TechX squad
proposed: Publish one P5 contract story for the case documents operations (or extend RWB-P5-E1024-APP with a contract part) before the SIT run, and name the rwb_document login in the DB story of the service.

title: The scan operation path of the RWB-P5-E1041-CON malware-scan contract is not specified
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 (rwb-document); TSD P5 Document hub v2 T-A.1; FSD P5 Document hub v3 A2.18
description: The upload must call the malware scan before the store, but no source names the path, verb or request and response shape of that operation. TSD P5 v2 T-A.1 lists no scan endpoint and the FSD describes the scan as a step, not as an API. RWB-P5-E1041-CON is the contract story that will fix it.
evidence: TSD P5 v2 T-A.1 endpoint inventory (API-P5-001 to API-P5-017) contains no scan endpoint; FSD P5 v3 A2.18 states the scan runs before storage with no interface named.
owner_role: Solution architect, with the P5 TechX squad
proposed: Fix the scan operation in RWB-P5-E1041-CON (path, request, response CLEAN/INFECTED, error shape) and build this story against its fake until then.

title: The SCR-30 route specification in the gateway-bff composite route is not specified
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 10 and 11; Template and Rules v1 DP-19
description: Architecture v5 slide 10 says the Documents tab loads from rwb-document, one hop, and DP-19 makes gateway-bff the route owner, but no source names the browser route path for SCR-30, the screen-model fields gateway-bff merges, or the per-call timeout and breaker values of that composite route.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 10 names the tab and the owner only; slide 11 fixes the 2 s REST budget but not the route; the API Specification has no gateway-bff screen route for SCR-30.
owner_role: Solution architect, with the gateway-bff squad
proposed: Publish the SCR-30 composite route in RWB-PLT-N001-CON with its path, merged fields and budget, and read this tab from it.

title: Producer-side AsyncAPI and JSON schema of rwb.document.events.v1 are not assigned to a contract story
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 (AsyncAPI 3.0 and JSON Schema registry, backward compatible) and slide 16 (P5 OUT: topic rwb.document.events.v1, DocumentStored, DocumentFieldsExtracted); TSD P5 v2 T3.1 and T5.3; FSD P5 v3 A2.1 AC-P5-001-01 (DocumentStored written to the outbox with the document ID, the case ID, the type and the source); Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-09 and DP-14
section: Contract 12.3; Solution plan; Out of scope
description: The trigger event of this slice is produced against a contract that no story of this run owns: the plan has no CON story for the P5 topic, so the producer-side AsyncAPI document, the registered JSON schema with its field names, types and required set, and the BACKWARD-compatibility rule for rwb.document.events.v1 are not fixed anywhere. The payload fields used here are restated from TSD P5 T3.1 and Architecture v5 slide 16 and validated by the schema registry story of the platform, so the build can proceed; a rename or an addition before the schema is registered would break the TRANSFER trigger fixture of RWB-P3-E1021-CON without an early warning.
evidence: No CON slice for rwb-document exists in _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json; Architecture v5 slide 11 requires AsyncAPI 3.0 per topic and a JSON Schema registry, and slide 16 names the events but not their fields; TSD P5 T5.3 lists the two published events with no payload
proposed: Publish the producer-side AsyncAPI 3.0 document of rwb.document.events.v1 with the registered JSON schema for rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 and rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1, its required fields and its BACKWARD-compatibility rule, as a P5 contract baseline story or as part of the deployment story of the service, and hand the DocumentStored schema to RWB-P3-E1021-CON as the trigger fixture

title: Per-service login name for rwb-document is not specified
source: Template and Rules v1 §R4 (one login per service) and §R5.5 DP-02; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 and slide 8 notes (19 rwb_* schemas, one login each); legacy story RWB-E1-021 precondition on the service login
description: The target rule is one database login per service and one schema per service, and the legacy story names a single shared login. No source document gives the login name for rwb-document, its grant set or its secret reference, so this story and its sibling P5 stories name it as a phrase and cannot create the login and its grants from the documents alone.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 §R4 and §R5.5 DP-02 state the rule but not the value; Architecture v5 slide 41 and slide 8 notes give the count of logins and schemas only; the legacy story precondition names the shared login only
proposed: Allocate the rwb-document login name, its grants (schema rwb_document only, no privilege on another schema) and its secret reference in the database story of the epic (RWB-PLT-NF06-DB and the P5 database story) and record them in the service catalogue

title: The rwb-document login name, the not-found message ID of the case read and the case-read field names are not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 4, 8 and 16 (one login per service; key caseId); TSD P5 Document hub v2 appendix T-A; legacy story RWB-E1-018 sections 12 and 14; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-02 and DP-11, R9
section: Story; Preconditions; Contract 12.2 and 12.8; Validation and messages
description: Three values this slice needs are missing from every source read. (1) The architecture fixes one database login per service but names no rwb-document login, grants or pool size. (2) The legacy story gives MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003, MSG-P7-003 and MSG-P3-025 but no message ID for a case the case service does not return, and the P3 contract story has not yet published one, so the 404 answer of the case read has no ID. (3) The legacy published interface gives the CaseView fields but the REST request and response field names of GET /cases/{caseId} are not fixed in the TSD P5, the FSD P5 or the legacy section 12.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 4 (every service: schema rwb_<name> + DB login) and slide 8 notes (19 Recovery schemas, one login and connection pool each); TSD P5 Document hub v2 T-A.1 and T-A.2 (document operations only, no case read); legacy story RWB-E1-018 section 12 (Endpoints table gives Case fields, not the REST field names) and section 14 (no 404 message ID); no login name in the Ownership Map or the P5 TSD
owner_role: Solution architect with the ACE DB team
proposed: The rwb_document DB story names the login and its grants under DP-02; the RWB-P3-E1018-CON contract publishes the case-read request and response field names and the not-found message ID, which this story then cites in place of the placeholder

title: The load, approve and in-force read shapes for document types are not specified
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-025 sections 4, 12 and 13 (the load went through the P4 POST /admin/reference-loads surface and the P5 ReferenceTableLoader interface); TSD P5 v2 appendix T-A (no document-type admin operation); TSD P5 v2 T3.1 (fields only); arch v5 slide 16 (rwb-document IN has documents and generate, no admin load)
section: Contract 12.1 and 12.2; Solution plan (Configuration and reference data)
description: The target makes P5 the owner that serves the load, the approve and the read of the document-type version in force under /api/recovery/document/v1, but no source gives the path segments, the request and response field names and types, the row-error shape of a refused load, the shape of the reference-version registration call it makes to the rwb-case reference-data contract, or the load-file template column layout. The story fixes the behaviour (statuses, the refuse-whole rule, the two-person rule, the valid-from rule, the legacy error codes) and leaves the shapes to the contract, so a caller or a test cannot be written from the documents alone.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-025 section 12 names request fields only for the P4 surface (multipart file, table, validFrom) and section 12.2 names no rwb-document admin path; TSD P5 v2 appendix T-A lists API-P5-001 to API-P5-017 with no document-type admin operation; the ownership map api section holds no /admin/document-types entry
proposed: Publish the document-type admin surface in the rwb-document OpenAPI 3.1 document (paths, request and response schemas, row-error schema, error codes) and the load template columns, and add the reference-version registration operation to the rwb-case reference-data contract, before the wave-1 integration harness of RWB-ITG-E1025-ITG runs

title: No role holds Reference data A to approve a document-type load
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-025 section 10 (the permission matrix gives Reference data A to no role; assumed granted to the legal counsel who owns the table, DL01); legacy section 3 (the approver holds Reference data A); TSD P5 v2 T6.1 (RW-LEGAL has CRUA on documents, RW-HEADNPA has R)
description: The two-person rule needs a second person who holds Reference data A, and the permission matrix gives that right to no role. The legacy story assumes the grant goes to the legal counsel who owns the type table, and this story carries the assumption: the approver in the tests holds Reference data A, and the production grant is still open. Until it is decided, a load in a non-test environment has no named approver role, so the approve step cannot be granted from the documents.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-025 section 10 row for the approver with Reference data A; legacy section 3 bullet on the loader and approver rights; TSD P5 v2 T6.1 gives RW-LEGAL CRUA and RW-HEADNPA R on documents, neither of which names the reference-data right
proposed: Decide in DL01 which role holds Reference data A for the document-type table (the assumed answer is the legal counsel who owns the table) and record it in the rwb-access permission matrix; if the Head of NPA is intended as the approver, grant the right there instead
